original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset'(n), the largest number such that every n-point planar set contains a subset of that size which spans no isosceles triangles.
target_in_paper: Section 6, the Brass-Moser-Pach open problem on the largest guaranteed subset of an n-point planar set that spans no isosceles triangles; in the June 7, 2014 PDF version of the same paper this is stated as Problem 25 and defines subset'(n) explicitly, while the current arXiv v3 HTML presents the same item in Section 6 as Problem 26. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem very closely: it asks for the asymptotic value of the same extremal function, uses the correct universal guarantee over all n-point planar sets, and identifies the forbidden configuration correctly as isosceles triangles. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the Euclidean plane R^2, with P a finite set of exactly n points. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

The extremal definition should be phrased exactly as a maximum guaranteed subset size: every P ⊂ R^2 with |P| = n contains a subset of size subset'(n) (equivalently, at least subset'(n)) that spans no isosceles triangles. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

To make the problem fully stand-alone, say explicitly that the asymptotic question concerns the growth of subset'(n) as n → ∞. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Unlike the later discussion of the function φ(n,3,3), this subset'(n) problem is not accompanied by an explicit convention about counting degenerate collinear isosceles triples, so that convention should not be silently added. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
refined_question: Let subset'(n) be the largest integer with the following property: every finite set P ⊂ R^2 with |P| = n contains a subset P' ⊂ P of size at least subset'(n) such that no three points of P' span an isosceles triangle. Determine the asymptotic growth of subset'(n) as n → ∞. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
justification: This is the exact open problem your draft is aiming at. The paper first defines subset'(n) as the maximum number guaranteed in every n-point planar set for a subset with no isosceles triangles, and then states the official problem: find the asymptotic value of subset'(n). The immediately following context gives the paper's nearby bounds, namely the trivial upper bound subset'(n) ≤ s(n) = O(sqrt(n)/(log n)^(1/4)) and the lower bound subset'(n) = Ω(n^0.4315) obtained by adapting Theorem 5.1, confirming that this is the intended narrow target and not the different later problem about the minimum number of distinct distances in isosceles-triangle-free sets. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
